source.title: Your AI Agent Is Hiding Its Mistakes From You
source.creator: AI Engineer

overview: Ben Holmes of Warp demonstrates how inspecting agent conversations, tool traces and score rubrics can expose repeated failures that successful task completion conceals.
whyItMatters: Agent teams can mistake a successful final result for efficient, reliable execution. Hidden retries, stale environment instructions, unnecessary tests and excessive tool calls can consume time and money without appearing in the result.
ghostMeshTakeaway: Sample comparable GhostMesh execution receipts for one recurring failure, correct its responsible instruction, then compare accepted outcomes and total cost before adopting a standing grading and self-repair system.

sourceInspection.method: Verified private ReasonPack with locally transcribed timed Whisper VTT and independent read-only cue review.
sourceInspection.caveat: Automated speech recognition is a timing aid, not certified speech or a replication of the vendor's internal run logs.
sourceInspection.publicationBoundary: Only original analysis and sanitized hashes appear in public Git; private media and transcripts remain in private custody.

custody.note: Verified source manifest and timed VTT retained privately on Hyperion; the public artifact contains only digests and qualified source descriptions.

normalization.falsification: Reject the proposed change if a comparable before-and-after sample does not reduce repeated failed calls and total effort without sacrificing accepted outcomes, safety or review authority.
normalization.freshness: The source is a vendor presentation. The verified private ReasonPack and retained timed aid establish what was presented, not independent operational outcomes.

claims.proposition: Agents can complete tasks after avoidable retries caused by stale instructions.
claims.assessment: Presenter demonstrates an agent searching port numbers and correcting course. The retained transcript supports the spoken example, not independent Warp logs.
claims.limits: A verified private source pack supports the reported demonstration, but no independent production replication or controlled result is established.
claims.temporalScope: November 6 video and retained timed aid only.

claims.proposition: Agent conversations and tool traces can be graded for redundant tests, verbosity and efficiency.
claims.assessment: The video shows rubric-based grading. Its predictive validity for accepted engineering quality is not established.
claims.limits: A verified private source pack supports the reported demonstration, but no independent production replication or controlled result is established.
claims.temporalScope: November 6 video and retained timed aid only.

claims.proposition: Skill Doctor proposes targeted changes to instructions and configuration from repeated scored failures.
claims.assessment: The vendor demonstrates a proposal mechanism, but no independent controlled reduction in cost or regression is supplied.
claims.limits: A verified private source pack supports the reported demonstration, but no independent production replication or controlled result is established.
claims.temporalScope: November 6 video and retained timed aid only.

claims.proposition: A merged skill change coincided with a reported increase in efficiency scoring.
claims.assessment: The presenter associates an inflection with a merged change. Model, task-mix and rubric changes remain confounders.
claims.limits: A verified private source pack supports the reported demonstration, but no independent production replication or controlled result is established.
claims.temporalScope: November 6 video and retained timed aid only.

claims.proposition: Suggested self-improvement pull requests enter a human review inbox.
claims.assessment: The presentation shows a review boundary; that does not prove every proposed change is safe or economical.

relationships.reason: The earlier Reader identifies review and accepted delivery as bottlenecks after agent execution becomes cheap. This deconstruction exposes retries and tool-call waste hidden beneath a successful final result, making execution quality another measurable part of that bottleneck.

The cockpit Reader separates visible dashboards from durable operational control. This analysis applies that distinction to grading agents: score trends are observability, while reviewed instruction changes, rollback and accepted outcomes provide the control boundary.

normalization.relationshipDisposition: Two curated Reader comparisons and two separately labeled outbound SharePlane Works. These are editorial context, not independent corroboration of Warp's results or automatic SharePlane graph admission.

review.status: Independent source/editorial review accepted for owner consideration
review.scope: Exact authored copy, five corrected timed cues, privacy boundary and claim posture; generated-site UAT remains pending.
review.findings: The five cues match the retained Whisper aid; the argument is qualified and publication remains owner-gated.

revisionHistory.reason: Admit the owner-approved manuscript to existing draft review without asserting Production publication.

normalization.orderReason: New verified private-source deconstruction of hidden agent execution friction.

relationshipReview.rationale: Owner requested meaningful relationships. These two existing Readers supply distinct, source-specific comparisons about accepted work and control over execution, without implying independent validation of Warp's product assertions.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Code Is No Longer the Hard Part
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: The video illustrates why successful code generation can conceal expensive execution friction, extending the Work's thesis that review, judgment and operational integration become the binding constraints.

sharePlaneRelationships.title: The Application Is Disposable. The Context Is Not.
sharePlaneRelationships.reason: Changing an agent's skills based on prior runs requires durable context about instructions, decisions, evidence and rollback, directly connecting to the Work's argument for persistent authority beyond replaceable applications.

sharePlaneReview.rationale: Two published Work identities are admitted only as outbound editorial routes. Their artifact URLs currently resolve through legacy V3 redirects, which is disclosed; neither route is independent corroboration or a write to SharePlane's canonical graph.
